summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress: credentialing for staging, network/VPC readiness, and scheduling an initial performance run. Main unblockers are service account access and finalizing KMS choice; Redwood to provide SOW and benchmark scripts. Security had a few open questions around audit logs and data-at-rest encryption for the pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: OK everyone thanks for joining, we have about 40 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Sanjay Rao: Sanjay here.
[00:08] Elena Morales: Elena on platform.
[00:09] Liam O'Connor: Liam from security.
[00:11] Ethan Ross: Ethan from Redwood SE.
[00:12] Maya Patel: And Hannah is on for CSM. Fine, agenda — creds, staging gate, bench plan, open security Qs, next steps.
[00:28] Elena Morales: Quick status, infra team spun up the staging cluster, we need the service account for Redwood to run the smoke tests and the peering route table update. We also need to lock IPs for the firewall.
[00:41] Maya Patel: Got it. On the service account — do you want us to use token-based API keys or a short-lived assume-role pattern?
[00:47] Elena Morales: Prefer assume-role with STS, better for org policy. We can provide an IAM role ARN and trust policy.
[00:55] Ethan Ross: That's perfect, Redwood can support assume-role. We'll need the role ARN and a test STS endpoint; we'll walk through the trust mapping. We'll also need a small set of allowed S3 prefixes for caching if you plan to use prefix caching, but that's optional.
[01:10] Priya Singh: On caching — we probably won't enable prefix caching in staging, want to keep runs deterministic.
[01:16] Ethan Ross: Fair. For the benchmarks we'll run both cold and warm KV cache tests so you can see delta.
[01:24] Sanjay Rao: Timeline question — we want results before EoD Friday so we can prep exec summary for next week. Is that feasible?
[01:31] Maya Patel: If creds are in by Tuesday we can schedule a 2-hour benchmark Wednesday/Thursday. We'll aim to deliver a runbook and initial report by Friday.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: Security items — SOC2 in place, we saw Redwood's attestation doc but need clarification on KMS. Are we sending keys to Redwood or using our own KMS via customer-managed keys?
[01:50] Hannah Li: Redwood supports customer-managed keys with HSM/KMS integrations; we do not require you to hand over raw keys. We have an integration guide, we'll share.
[01:58] Liam O'Connor: And audit logs? Need chain-of-custody for inference requests, retention policy for logs, and proof we can export logs to our SIEM.
[02:08] Ethan Ross: We can stream audit logs via secure webhook or S3 export; retention defaults to 90 days on hosted but for dedicated pilot we can adjust retention or stream to your SIEM. We'll attach the log export config doc.
[02:19] Elena Morales: Network — peering done but we haven't set NAT gateway IP whitelisting. We need a static egress for Redwood callbacks.
[02:26] Maya Patel: We can recommend using a NAT with elastic IPs; Redwood can also accept a CIDR allowlist, provide the staging IPs once peering is validated.
[02:36] Priya Singh: Also curious about latency SLOs — what should we expect on dedicated variant with batch size=1?
[02:43] Ethan Ross: Rough ballpark depends on model; for the 7B quantized variant you're likely to see 40–80ms p50 and 120–250ms p95 under light concurrency, but we'll validate with your prompt set.
[02:55] Sanjay Rao: If p95 is high, can we fall back to a cheaper hosted model during spikes?
[03:00] Maya Patel: Yes, routing policies can be configured: primary dedicated, fallback hosted or lower-cost model. We'll show routing config in the console.
[03:08] Liam O'Connor: On data protection: are inputs persisted anywhere? We need to know what is stored for debugging and for quality monitoring.
[03:14] Ethan Ross: For the pilot we can disable long-term retention; short-lived logs for troubleshooting retained 7 days unless otherwise configured. We'll include that in the SOW.
[03:23] Elena Morales: Any friction with our on-prem connectors? We're running parts of our stack on-prem and some data can't leave the VPC.
[03:29] Maya Patel: Redwood Private supports VPC-only routing and on-prem packages; for the pilot you can keep sensitive data in VPC and send only necessary payloads to the inference endpoint. We should map which data elements are PII.
[03:40] Priya Singh: We'll provide a mapping doc.
[03:42] Ethan Ross: Ok great. Bench plan overview — we'll run a three-phase test: connectivity & auth smoke, single-client latency sweep with golden prompts, then ramp to concurrency run to measure throughput and observe autoscaling. We recommend 5–10 prompts representative of your workload.
[03:57] Sanjay Rao: We'll convert 8 canonical prompts from production traces and sanitize them.
[04:02] Maya Patel: Excellent. Who will own creating that prompt set?
[04:05] Sanjay Rao: Elena will own prompt set creation.
[04:07] Elena Morales: Yep I'll do that.
[04:09] Maya Patel: Great — Ethan will prepare the benchmark scripts and a sample results dashboard.
[04:14] Ethan Ross: I'll also include instructions for running locally with your service account and the exact metrics we capture: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, cache hit rate.
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: On encryption in transit — we need mTLS for service-to-service comms. Does Redwood support mTLS for private deployments?
[04:32] Ethan Ross: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support mutual TLS; for hosted API we rely on TLS with client cert options for premium plans. We'll capture specifics in the security appendix.
[04:42] Maya Patel: Anything else on compliance?
[04:44] Liam O'Connor: Just a final ask — we need to confirm who has access to the audit logs and who can request log exports; might require a role mapping.
[04:52] Hannah Li: We'll include an RBAC mapping template.
[04:55] Priya Singh: One small thing — will Redwood provide a sample config for autoscaling thresholds? We're inclined to limit burst to control costs.
[05:02] Ethan Ross: Yes, the default policy is CPU/GPU util and request latency; you'll get a recommended config tuned for your latency SLO and cost target. For pilot we'll default to conservative autoscale to prevent cost surprises.
[05:14] Sanjay Rao: Ok sounds good.
[05:16] Maya Patel: Recap then: Redwood to send SOW + pricing + security appendix; Ethan to upload bench scripts and sample dashboard; Nimbus to provision service account & IAM role and create prompt set; Security to confirm KMS preference and audit log requirements. We'll try to bench mid-next-week and deliver an initial report by Friday.
[05:36] Elena Morales: One more quick question — can the bench test emulate session state so we can measure KV cache benefits?
[05:41] Ethan Ross: Yes we have scripts for cold vs warm cache; we can run both and show delta; will need to seed cache for warm run.
[05:49] Maya Patel: Perfect. Any final blockers?
[05:52] Liam O'Connor: None from security besides the docs ask.
[05:54] Priya Singh: No blockers.
[05:55] Sanjay Rao: Good, thanks all.
[05:57] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and links.

Notes/Links shared during call:
- Staging runbook (link provided in chat)
- Redwood security appendix (to be emailed)
- Benchmark script repo (will be shared by Ethan)

Recording ends.
